name: Life Positions & the OK Corral
oneLine: Four basic stances toward self and others - OK/not-OK crossed with OK/not-OK - that we cycle through all day, with one favorite quadrant we return to.
whatYouDid: You watched Diego shift through Get-Rid-Of, Get-On-With, and the rest of Ernst's OK Corral across one ordinary shift, in both Adult and scripty versions of the same operation.
confusion: Position as a mood rather than a decision

fromBook.quote: Though we switch between quadrants on the Corral, we each have one 'favorite' quadrant where we spend most of our time while in script.

expand.definition: Life position is one's basic belief about self and others, used to justify decisions and behavior. Franklin Ernst's OK Corral maps the four combinations (I'm OK/You're OK, I'm not-OK/You're OK, I'm OK/You're not-OK, I'm not-OK/You're not-OK) onto four social operations: Get-On-With, Get-Away-From, Get-Rid-Of, and Get-Nowhere-With.
expand.otherFraming: Berne thought the early decision comes first and the life position is adopted later to justify it; Steiner thought the position (starting from 'basic trust') comes first and the decisions follow. TA Today presents both without picking a winner.
expand.tryThisToday: Sketch your own Corralogram tonight: which quadrant got the most square inches of your actual day, and what Adult operation could you have used there instead?
